definitions.explanation: The nut of an oak tree. A familiar sight in autumn in Japan, often collected by children.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{公園|こうえん}で{団栗|どんぐり}を{集|あつ}めている。
examples.english: The children are collecting acorns in the park.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{山道|やまみち}にたくさんの{団栗|どんぐり}が{落|お}ちている。
examples.english: In autumn, many acorns lie scattered on the mountain paths.

notes:
IDIOM:
{団栗|どんぐり}の{背比|せくら}べ literally means "height comparison among acorns" — used to describe people or things that are all much the same with no clear winner. Similar to English "much of a muchness."

USAGE:
Usually written in hiragana as どんぐり. The kanji {団栗|どんぐり} is rarely used in everyday writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {団栗|どんぐり}を{拾|ひろ}う: to pick up acorns
- {団栗|どんぐり}の{背比|せくら}べ: all much the same, no standout
- {団栗|どんぐり}{拾|ひろ}い: acorn gathering
